/guides/image-to-perler.description: Learn how to upload an image, choose MARD colors, edit layers, and export PNG or PDF bead charts.
/guides/image-to-perler.content:
FROM IMAGE TO PATTERN

How to turn an image into a bead pattern

Use Perler Beads Generator to convert an image into an editable grid, then export a pattern chart and a materials list.

  1. Upload an image: Open the editor and choose a clear subject with a simple background.
  2. Set the size: Choose a width; image height follows its aspect ratio. Simple silhouettes work at smaller sizes, while detailed pictures usually need more cells.
  3. Choose style and colors: Cartoon style favors clear color blocks; realistic style preserves tonal changes. A lower color limit simplifies supplies but can remove detail.
  4. Review the pattern: Refine edges with drawing tools and layers. Check the isolated bead warning.
  5. Export: Download PNG or PDF charts, an Excel materials list, or a JSON project to continue editing later.

Original image and generated chart

This cartoon example comes from the project documentation. Results depend on image, size, background settings, and color limit; exact generation settings are not recorded here.

Is the original image uploaded?

Conversion and editing happen in your browser. If you publish a pattern to the marketplace, its pattern data is sent to the server and a preview becomes public.

/guides/mard-colors.title: MARD Color Matching & Bead Usage Guide
/guides/mard-colors.description: Understand MARD palettes, color limits, layer counts, and pack estimates when preparing a bead project.
/guides/mard-colors.content:
COLORS & SUPPLIES

MARD colors and bead usage

The editor includes the MARD Basic 221 and Complete 291 color palettes. Image conversion matches the built-in palette; you can then adjust individual color codes.

How many colors should I use?

Fewer colors usually produce a simpler design with fewer supplies. More colors preserve additional shades. Review a small preview and refine the pattern using colors you have available.

How is usage counted?

The editor counts each color across layers marked for inclusion in usage. Packs are calculated by dividing the bead count by beads per pack and rounding up. For example, 650 beads with 500 beads per pack requires an estimated 2 packs. Included overlapping layers are counted separately; public marketplace totals count the visible composite image.

Why do physical beads look different?

Screens, lighting, and manufacturing batches affect appearance. Palette matching is a creative aid, not a guarantee of an exact physical color match. Check the actual brand codes and beads.

Can I view a shared pattern’s colors?

Previews and basic information are public. Sign in to see detailed color counts, open the pattern in the editor, or download JSON. Local editor exports do not require signing in.

/about.title: About Perler Beads Generator
/about.description: Learn about this online bead pattern editor, its open-source origins, and supported features.
/about.content:
About Perler Beads Generator

An online tool for converting images into bead patterns, drawing by hand, working with layers, and exporting charts and materials lists.

This site builds on the open-source Perler Beads Generator project. See source code and issue reporting and the upstream project. MARD identifies the palette used for matching and does not imply an official partnership.

No installation is needed for local editing. Share only images and patterns you have permission to publish.

/privacy.title: Privacy & Data
/privacy.description: Learn about local image processing, public patterns, account sessions, and visitor statistics.
/privacy.content:
Privacy and data

Images and drafts

Image conversion and editing happen in your browser. Drafts are stored in the current browser; clearing storage may remove them. Export JSON backups to keep your work.

Public sharing

Publishing a pattern sends the pattern and its description to the server. Preview images, titles, author usernames, and basic information are public. Full pattern data, detailed colors, editing, and downloads require sign-in.

Accounts and sessions

The server stores salted password hashes and session token hashes, not plain-text passwords. An HttpOnly cookie keeps you signed in for up to 7 days.

Visitor statistics

A random browser identifier is used to count page views, visitors, tab sessions, referring domains, and feature use. Application analytics do not store raw IP addresses, original images, passwords, or canvas content. Hosting and database providers may keep infrastructure logs under their own policies.

Clear browser storage to reset the visitor identifier, or sign out to revoke the current session. Self-service password recovery and account deletion are not currently available. Do not put sensitive information in public pattern descriptions.

A few things before you start

Do I need an account?

Local image conversion, editing, and exports work without signing in. Publishing, detailed marketplace color usage, opening shared patterns, and JSON downloads require an account.

Which export formats are supported?

PNG and PDF charts, Excel materials lists, and editable JSON project files.

Are my images uploaded?

Conversion and editing happen in your browser. Only patterns you actively publish to the marketplace are sent to the server.

Will physical bead colors match the screen?

The palette is a matching aid. Screens, lighting, and manufacturing batches affect color; check actual beads before preparing supplies.
